Run Simulation

Run a full year (365 days, 8760 hours) P2P energy sharing simulation. PV Flow: PV DC → Inverter (PAC = PDC × η) → Load/Battery. P2P Logic: PV priority → Battery (stops at 20% SoC) → P2P pool (SoC threshold) → Grid. Each household has independent demand variation. Battery sharing is capped daily per household's assigned %.

Run a simulation first to see reports.

P2P Value Threshold Analysis

Sweeps PV size (0.5×–3× current) and battery count (1–5 units) across all 6 households simultaneously, running 50 full-year simulations to identify where P2P trading peaks and where it becomes financially significant. Each run uses deterministic demand for reproducibility. Note: P2P peaks around 1.0–1.25× PV (where some households have surplus while others still have deficit), then declines as all households become self-sufficient — this is a key finding about when P2P has the most value.

%
📋 Input Guide
Field Suggested Value What it does & when to use it
P2P Threshold
% of demand traded		 1 – 2% Low sensitivity. Flags even marginal P2P activity. Use if your households have small PV systems or you want to detect the earliest point where any trading begins.
P2P Threshold
% of demand traded		 3 – 5% ✅ Recommended. A meaningful signal that P2P is genuinely contributing — not just occasional micro-transfers. Balanced between sensitivity and significance.
P2P Threshold
% of demand traded		 10%+ High bar. Only use if you want P2P to be a dominant energy source. May never be reached if PV sizing is modest.
LCOE Gap Threshold
₱/kWh saved via P2P		 ₱0.01 – 0.05 Very low bar. Triggers even if P2P saves very little per kWh. Useful for exploratory analysis or when your grid tariff is low.
LCOE Gap Threshold
₱/kWh saved via P2P		 ₱0.10 – 0.50 ✅ Recommended. Roughly 1–5% of a typical ₱10/kWh grid tariff. Ensures P2P is delivering a financially noticeable saving. Adjust upward if your grid price is high.
LCOE Gap Threshold
₱/kWh saved via P2P		 ₱1.00+ High bar. Only if you want P2P to deliver very substantial savings — close to or exceeding the grid tariff itself. May never trigger at typical PV sizes.
💡 Tip: Both conditions must be met simultaneously to flag the threshold. Run once with default values, check the results table for your actual peak P2P % and LCOE gap, then set thresholds to about 70% of those peak values to mark the meaningful sweet spot.
